Restaurant food sales.text: Restaurant Food Sales . Restaurant revenue generated from the sale of food, including non-alcoholic beverages, at restaurants totaled $34,608,000 for the thirteen weeks ended March 28, 2026 as compared to $32,586,000 for the thirteen weeks ended March 29, 2025. This increase in restaurant food sales is attributable to the Recent Price Increases and increased restaurant traffic. Comparable weekly restaurant food sales for restaurants open for all of the thirteen weeks ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025 respectively, which consists of eleven restaurants owned by us and ten restaurants owned by affiliated limited partnerships was $2,635,000 and $2,481,000 for the thirteen weeks ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively, an increase of 6.21%. Comparable weekly restaurant food sales for Company-owned restaurants was $1,304,000 and $1,235,000 for the thirteen weeks ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively, an increase of 5.59%. Comparable weekly restaurant food sales for affiliated limited partnership owned restaurants only was $1,331,000 and $1,246,000 for the thirteen weeks ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively, an increase of 6.82%. We expect that restaurant food sales, including non-alcoholic beverages, for the balance of our fiscal year 2026 will increase due to the Recent Price Increases.

opex.text: Operating Expenses . Operating expenses (including but not limited to utilities, insurance, cleaning, credit card fees, supplies, security, and other costs closely related to running restaurant and package operations) for our fiscal year 2025 increased $2,737,000 or 11.08% to $27,438,000 from $24,701,000 for our fiscal year 2024 due primarily to the operation of our Company-owned restaurant in Hollywood, Florida (Store #19R) for our full fiscal year 2025 as opposed to part of our fiscal year 2024, inflation and otherwise due to increases in expenses across all categories.

costs.text: Costs and Expenses . lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
